subject: SLO probing runbook & staffing checklist
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Ava Townsend <ava.t@trustline.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: network probing runbook + next steps

Hi Ava / Rajesh —

Thanks again for the demo today. Per our conversation, Trustline's streaming use case (real-time triage transcripts) has two gating items we need to validate on your side before we can finalize the Dedicated/private deployment plan:

1) sustained ingress/egress throughput at 1.5 Gbps for 30-minute windows (burst to 3 Gbps)
2) tail latency target for streaming tokens: <= 120ms 95th for in-region traffic
3) support for 1,200 concurrent open streaming sessions with KV cache affinity

I captured an initial probing runbook and a lightweight staffing checklist (attached) — it's a template we use for customer network preflight. Can you confirm who on your networking team will own running the probes? Ideally we get one internal owner and one SRE to shadow the first validation run.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Trustline runs the attached probe plan against the VPN/peering path by EOD next Thursday (May 27)
- We (Redwood) will run an independent probe window on May 28 to correlate traces
- If traces look good, schedule a 30-min troubleshooting window to tune MTU and TCP settings (if needed)

Attachments: network_probe_template.xlsx (probe steps), sample-traces-05-19.zip (example traces from a similar customer)

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks Naomi —

I shared the probe plan with our network lead (Rajesh) and our SRE, Lina. Rajesh will run the initial probe; Lina will stand by to watch the traces. Two quick notes:
- We currently have a reserved egress of 1 Gbps in our AWS transit gateway for this app. We can temporarily increase to 2 Gbps for the test but need to confirm with procurement.
- Our current VPN uses AES-256-GCM and routes through a transit VPC with an extra NAT hop; we want to understand how that extra hop impacts tail latency during streaming.

We can commit to running the probes on Thursday (May 27) in the 09:00–11:00 PT window. I'll send a calendar invite with the team shortly.

Ava Townsend

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Ava Townsend <ava.t@trustline.health>, Rajesh Singh <rajesh@trustline.health>
Date: Fri, 20 May 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: network probing runbook + next steps

On Thu, May 19, 2027 at 4:18 PM Ava Townsend <ava.t@trustline.health> wrote:
> Thanks Naomi —
> I shared the probe plan with our network lead (Rajesh) and our SRE, Lina.

Thanks for the quick reply, Ava — a couple of technical clarifications from the Redwood side before the probe run:

1) Probe endpoints: please run both a long-lived streaming session probe (30s+ continuous token flow) and a short burst probe (10s at 3 Gbps) to capture behavior under both steady-state and burst.
2) Packet captures: capture at the transit gateway and the VPN endpoint (if different). We want TCP RTT and per-packet timestamping to compute tail behavior.
3) MTU/TCP settings: if there is an extra NAT hop, please record MSS observed and any fragmentation. We will also test UDP-based heartbeats to compare overhead of TLS over TCP.
4) Trace naming: use the following naming convention for traces: TL_PROBE_<date>_<probe-type> (e.g., TL_PROBE_20270527_stream30s) — this will help us correlate.

If you can drop the sample captures into the Drive folder I shared, Mateo and I will run automated parsers overnight and get a summary before your run.

-Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ava Townsend <ava.t@trustline.health>
Cc: Rajesh Singh <rajesh@trustline.health>
Date: Mon, 21 May 2027 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: network probing runbook + next steps

Thanks all — small operational checklist from Redwood for the May 27 window:

- Redwood engineer on standby: Mateo (08:30–11:30 PT)
- Probe types: streaming_30s, burst_10s (3Gbps), control_plane_heartbeat (1s interval)
- Required artifacts from Trustline: packet captures (pcap), iperf logs, traceroute outputs to our egress IP (listed in the Drive doc)
- Acceptance quick pass: throughput >= 1.5 Gbps sustained for 30 mins (we will mark provisional pass if sustained for 20 of 30 minutes during test window)
- Latency pass: 95th percentile streaming token latency <= 120ms when tested from Trustline's primary region to Redwood's us-west cluster

I'll also attach a small runbook snippet for the post-probe triage (where to look for retransmits, zero-window stalls, and gso/segmentation artifacts).

Attachment: network_probe_template.xlsx

-Mateo
Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

> Thanks all — small operational checklist from Redwood for the May 27 window:

All set on our side. Lina will run the iperf and packet captures on May 27 at 09:00 PT and upload the artifacts to the Drive folder. Procurement confirmed a temporary increase to 2 Gbps for that window.

Two items for Redwood to confirm before we run:
1) please share the exact egress IPs we'll target (so we can update firewall allowlist)
2) can Redwood confirm whether the test should run over the production transit GW path or via a direct VPN tunnel to the Redwood private egress (we'd prefer the path that matches expected production routing)

If you can confirm both today we will lock the probe schedule.

Thanks —
